summary: Connects two-dimensional or higher-dimensional arrangements of primitives or points into triangle or quad meshes. It can skin all primitives, groups of N primitives, or skip every Nth primitive, and can close the resulting mesh.

key_params.name: skinops
key_params.note: All primitives, groups of N primitives, or skip every Nth primitive

key_params.name: inc
key_params.note: N value for grouped or skipped skinning

key_params.name: closed
key_params.note: Connect the last vertex back to the first

key_concepts: Skin POP connects a two-dimensional or higher-dimensional POP point arrangement into a mesh of triangles or quads.
POP Dimension metadata is central: rows and columns define how points are connected, independent of how the input primitives were originally wired.
For three or more dimensions, skinning applies to the first two dimensions and repeats across the higher dimensions.
Skin mode can use all primitives, groups of N primitives, or skip every Nth primitive when dimensions alone are not the desired grouping.
Closed connects the last vertex back to the first, and Output Quads preserves quad mesh structure instead of triangulating.
common_gotchas: Skin POP uses POP dimensions heavily; inspect or set dimensions before skinning ambiguous inputs.
For inputs with three or more dimensions, skinning applies over the first two dimensions and repeats across higher dimensions.
Output quads preserve grid structure better; triangles may be preferable for render compatibility.
